subject: Execution plan for DPA + UK addendum / SCCs — signing and subprocessor confirmation
messages:

Cc: Ben Lee <ben.lee@medicore.com>, DataTrust Legal <privacy@datatrust.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: DPA + transfer terms question (SCCs / UK addendum)

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks promising for our diagnostics pipeline. Procurement and legal asked me to follow up on a couple of items so we can get the Data Processing Agreement (DPA) over the finish line:

- We need confirmation Redwood will execute EC SCCs (2021 or updated modular) or sign the UK IDTA addendum if we route UK patient data.
- Procurement needs a redline showing any deviations from our standard DPA; we prefer DocuSign execution but can accept Adobe Sign.
- A list of current subprocessors and whether any subprocessors process data in jurisdictions outside the EEA/UK — specifically if any US-based analytic providers get access to raw content.

Can you share a signing timeline and an initial redline? We’re aiming to have the legal review completed by 2026-04-07.

Appreciate it —
Aisha
Procurement, Medicore Health

Attachment: Medicore_DPA-questions.pdf (stub)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA + transfer terms question (SCCs / UK addendum)

Hi Aisha —

Great to hear — thanks for the clear list. Quick plan:

1) I’ve attached our working redline (Redwood_DPA-Redlines-v3.docx) that accepts the EC SCCs + includes an optional UK IDTA addendum clause (we’ll toggle to execute the IDTA when UK-resident personal data is in scope).
2) Subprocessor matrix attached (Subprocessor-Matrix-20260324.xlsx) — rows show location and data access level. We do use a US analytics vendor for usage telemetry but they only receive pseudonymized/aggregated telemetry; no raw patient PHI leaves the EEA/UK.
3) We can do DocuSign for execution. I’ll coordinate with legal to finalize the envelope; target DocuSign send by 2026-03-30 so you can get it signed before your April 7 deadline.

Looping in Karthik from Legal (for legal comments) and Marissa on account/contract ops for signature cadence. Rishi — quick confirm on the telemetry processing detail above?

Next steps: I’ll incorporate any final legal redlines and email you the DocuSign link.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA-Redlines-v3.docx (redline), Subprocessor-Matrix-20260324.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fw: DPA + transfer terms question (internal)

FYI — forwarding Medicore’s procurement questions. Key asks: SCCs/UK IDTA, redline + DocuSign, subprocessor jurisdiction details.

Karthik: main legal points to watch in the redline:
- Transfer mechanism language (we currently propose: EC SCCs + conditional IDTA addendum if UK data processed)
- Liability caps and residual data rights (they may push for carveouts for regulator requests)
- Audit / evidence: they asked for implementation evidence; we typically provide SOC 2 report + config screenshots, and can offer a 30-day evidence handover window for onboarding.

Marissa: if legal signs off, I want to get the envelope out on 3/30. Please prepare the commercial signature route and approve the DocuSign template.

Rishi: confirm telemetry is pseudonymized and stored in US analytics, and that we can provide the pseudonymization description in writing.

Thanks team —
Evelyn

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fw: DPA + transfer terms question (internal)

Thanks Evelyn — I reviewed Redwood_DPA-Redlines-v3.docx. High-level legal notes: 

- Transfer mechanism: the current wording referencing the 2021 EC SCCs is defensible; add a short fallback sentence that we will execute a UK addendum where UK law requires it. Avoid committing to a single "IDTA format" label — say "UK Addendum or equivalent mechanism" to keep flexibility.
- Subprocessors: good to include a commitment to notify customers of new subprocessors 30 days prior and offer procurement a chance to object on reasonable grounds. 
- Audit / evidence: provide SOC 2 Type II + a cropped screenshot export showing audit log retention default. For high-risk regulated customers, offer an evidence-sharing window (as Evelyn suggested).
- Liability: pushback likely — we should not open up additional carveouts for regulator requests beyond standard language. Keep cap as per commercial terms.

I’ll add inline comments in the redline and prepare a short legal cover note for the DocuSign envelope.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>

- Confirmed subprocessors: the attached matrix lists current providers and jurisdiction; the US analytics vendor receives only pseudonymized telemetry (no raw patient PHI).
- Evidence: we will attach SOC 2 Type II and can provide a screenshot export of audit/log retention for onboarding.
